quiz.q: According to Plato, what constitutes justice in the ideal state?
options: Each class strictly performs its natural duty without interfering in the functions of others
Citizens share political sovereignty equally through regular democratic voting in the popular assembly
Material wealth and private property are distributed with absolute equality among all social classes
Rulers govern strictly under written constitutional laws drafted and approved by the collective citizenry
quiz.why: Plato defines justice as non-interference and proper stationing, where each soul-based class fulfills its natural duty without encroaching upon others.

quiz.q: According to Plato, what is the primary purpose of the state-controlled education system?
options: To promote commercial prosperity by equipping artisans with specialized technical and trading skills
To determine individual aptitude and assign each citizen to their appropriate social class
To cultivate democratic citizens capable of rotating between ruling and being ruled in turn
To enforce total economic equality by eliminating natural intellectual differences among all citizens
quiz.why: Plato designs education as a screening mechanism to reveal each individual's innate aptitude and place them into their corresponding social class.

quiz.q: Why does Plato exclude the producer class from his system of communism?
options: Producers have naturally mastered their appetites and require no institutional rules against corruption
Aristotle convinced Plato that private property is indispensable for moral virtue and charitable acts
They hold no political power and cannot control their innate appetite for worldly pleasures
Soldiers and rulers require private farm estates to fund military expeditions and state administration
quiz.why: Plato exempts producers because they lack political power to corrupt the state and are dominated by appetite, making private property psychologically necessary.

quiz.q: What single constitutional limitation does Plato place on the absolute power of the philosopher king?
options: The ruler must submit all executive decrees to public opinion for democratic ratification
The ruler must govern strictly according to written books of statutory civil law
The ruler must share supreme legislative authority equally with a council of soldiers
The ruler cannot alter the fundamental constitution and established class structure of the republic
quiz.why: Although Plato frees the philosopher king from written laws and public opinion, the ruler is forbidden from changing the constitution of the republic.
